text:
Alex: Heads-up — seeing memory climb on a few hosts serving long Mistral-7B sessions. KV cache pages keep increasing after ~30k tokens and don't compact. dump attached -> pmap shows steady growth. :eyes:

Maria: Which model variant + runtime? any recent kernel changes?

Alex: mistral-7b-instruct with rope-scaling enabled (we use a dynamic rope rescale at 8k->64k when sessions hit extended context). Runtime: our custom C++ runtime + nvkernel v2 selection (falling back to cudnn kernels for some ops). Batching heuristics: default continuous-batching.

Alex: quick paste from one host (1h run):
```
kv_pages_before: 12032
kv_pages_after: 14788
fragmentation_ratio: 0.41
resident_kv_mem: 48.2GB -> 59.1GB
notes: no large spikes, slow linear growth correlates with rope rescale events
```

Chen: Interesting. Could be fragmentation + page alignment once rope rescale doubles effective sequence length. When we re-allocate new KV slices for extended contexts they end up on new pages and small leftover fragments aren't reused. Do we use page coalescing on free list?

Alex: We do a freelist with size buckets but pages are fixed 2MB. The issue looks like many allocations are slightly sub-page and never coalesce because they sit between active KV segments tied to different sessions, and sessions pin pages due to session-local token positions + sparse eviction.

Tim: profiling-bot: uploaded flamegraph and heapmap (link: https://internal/snapshots/1762506789/heapmap). Quick summary: hot path is kv_alloc + rope_rescale handler. Also a surprising hotspot in kernel-selection where we pick a cudnn fallback for rotary-scaled matmul, which emits slightly different memory strides leading to misaligned GPU buffers.

Sasha: Could the cudnn fallback be creating temporary buffers that get pinned and then folded into the KV allocator's ownership? I vaguely remember a similar issue with Qwen where MQA conversion left small pinned slices until next GC tick.

Chen: Right — Qwen/MQA vs GQA: when upstream model weights are MQA-quantized we have an extra re-order pass that creates small tensoreshard views. If rope rescale triggers recompile, those temporaries can be promoted into persistent caches by our legacy refcount path. For Mistral we also do a per-layer rope multiplier table which is stored per-session if rescale is triggered mid-session. That increases live allocations.

Maria: Can you reproduce with a deterministic harness? single worker, repeated sessions with rope rescale events, no other traffic?

Alex: Yes. Repro steps in thread:
1) Start single worker with kv page debug on.
2) Spawn 30 sessions that request long history and trigger rope rescale at token ~8192.
3) Wait 15 minutes. Observe kv_pages increase ~+20-25%.

Alex: I pushed a quick experiment: force compaction after rescale (call compact_free_pages(true)). Results in 2 runs:
- baseline: +22% pages after 1h
- +compaction: +6% pages after 1h, fragmentation_ratio down from 0.41 -> 0.12

Tim: Nice. Any perf impact? compaction could be expensive.

Alex: Compaction adds a small 80-150ms stall during the rescale window (we throttle it to not block inference). For our tail latency SLOs that's borderline but acceptable as a short-term mitigation.

Sasha: Long-term I'd prefer avoiding the promotion of temporaries into the global KV arena. Two ideas: (1) change kernel-selection so rotary/rescale uses our custom kernel (no fallback) to avoid creating temp strides; (2) change freelist to support in-place merging and a per-session slab for rescale transient allocations.

Chen: I prototyped a smaller change: when rope_rescale occurs, allocate rescale temp buffers from a per-rescale arena that gets freed atomically after operation. This avoids scattering small frees across the global freelist. Microbenchmark: reduces fragmentation by ~35% and no added stalls. Patch attached:
```diff
- auto* temp = global_kv_alloc(len);
+ auto* temp = rescale_arena.alloc(len);
 ...
- global_kv_free(temp);
+ // free later when rescale_arena.reset() runs
```

Maria: Can you run that in staging with the deterministic harness? also include Qwen 7B variant with MQA to compare.

Alex: Ran both:
- Mistral-7B + per-rescale-arena: pages +4% after 1h (vs +22% baseline)
- Qwen-7B-MQA (same harness): pages +9% baseline, +5% with patch. Qwen still worse initially due to MQA temporaries but patch helps.

Tim: Any kernel selection changes? If we can remove cudnn fallback we might eliminate stride-copy temporaries. But need to ensure our custom kernel has equal numeric fidelity.

Sasha: I'll take kernel work. Plan: port rotary-rescale path to custom kernel and add a fastpath when rope multiplier doesn't change per-layer. That should avoid recompiles + temporaries. Est ETA: 1 sprint.

Maria: Good. For short-term: enable compact_free_pages(true) gated behind an env var per-pool, and enable Chen's per-rescale-arena for Mistral pools. Monitor for regressions.

Alex: I'll roll out to two hosts in us-west for validation and report back. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment queued to us-west-test (2 hosts). change: enable rescale-arena + compaction env.

Alex: Quick follow-up (after 6h): rollout looks promising — one host shows stable KV after rescale events, memory plateaued. Will run 24h and share metrics. :party_parrot:
